[marimo](https://marimo.io) notebooks are reactive Python notebooks stored as plain `.py` files.
The notebook below runs in your browser: move a slider and the plot updates.

```{=html}
<iframe src="../assets/notebooks/explore-umap/index.html"
        title="Interactive marimo notebook: exploring UMAP parameters"
        loading="lazy"
        style="width: 100%; height: 1150px; border: 1px solid var(--bs-border-color, #e4e3df); border-radius: 8px;">
</iframe>
<p style="font-size: 0.85em; margin-top: 0.25rem;">
  <a href="../assets/notebooks/explore-umap/index.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the notebook in a new tab</a>
  (it takes a few seconds to load Python in your browser).
</p>
```

At its core, the notebook is two sliders and one polars-umap call:

```python
n_neighbors = mo.ui.slider(steps=[5, 15, 50, 200], value=15, label="n_neighbors")
min_dist = mo.ui.slider(steps=[0.0, 0.1, 0.5, 0.99], value=0.1, label="min_dist")

digits.umap.fit_transform(
    "pixels", n_neighbors=n_neighbors.value, min_dist=min_dist.value, random_state=42
)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Precomputed in the browser, live on your machine

The browser runs Python through WebAssembly (Pyodide). polars-umap is a compiled Rust extension
without a WebAssembly build, so in the browser the notebook shows a grid of embeddings that
polars-umap computed beforehand, with
[`scripts/precompute_notebook_data.py`](https://github.com/jeroenjanssens/polars-umap/blob/main/scripts/precompute_notebook_data.py).
On your own machine, it runs polars-umap live.
:::

## Run it locally

The notebook declares its dependencies inline
([PEP 723](https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/)), so marimo can install them in an isolated
environment:

```bash
uvx marimo edit --sandbox \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeroenjanssens/polars-umap/main/notebooks/explore-umap.py
```

Or, in a project that already has polars-umap:

```bash
uv add marimo altair scikit-learn
uv run marimo edit explore-umap.py
```

The source is in
[`notebooks/explore-umap.py`](https://github.com/jeroenjanssens/polars-umap/blob/main/notebooks/explore-umap.py).

## Using polars-umap in your own notebook

polars-umap needs nothing special in marimo. A UI element feeding its parameters makes the
embedding recompute whenever the element changes:

```python
import marimo as mo
import polars as pl
import polars_umap  # noqa: F401

n_neighbors = mo.ui.slider(2, 100, value=15, label="n_neighbors")
n_neighbors
```

```python
df.umap.fit_transform("embedding", n_neighbors=n_neighbors.value, random_state=0)
```

UMAP on a few thousand rows takes a fraction of a second, which keeps the notebook responsive.
For larger data, use `mo.ui.slider(..., debounce=True)` so the embedding only recomputes when
the slider is released.
